text:
maya: heads up — asia-northeast1 apiserver fd usage shot up during the GPU node drain, controller-manager requeue rate up ~3x. etcd leader sync latency moved from ~10ms -> ~2s. seeing a lot of TCP_FIN_WAIT on the proxy.
deploy-bot: deployed node-drainer v2.3.1 at 1778898950 (rollout: canary 10%).
dylan: ugh. did we do a rolling drain across all GPU pools at once? that can cause conn churn + SNAT exhaustion.
maya: yeah we kicked off drain for gpu-pool-asia to rebalance. policy was maxUnavailable=30% across the pool, but the pool is small (~12 nodes) so we had two drains concurrently.
sam: can you paste socket stats from the proxy host? also apiserver logs for "connection reset"?
maya: pasted short grep below:
```
proxy-conntrack: tcp_inuse=2456 tcp_max=2600
apiserver: apiserver_request_total{code="503"} 42
etcd: raft.appendEntriesDuration_seconds_sum 2.1
```
jess: 2456 in-use sockets is scary on a single nat gateway. if SNAT ports get exhausted we'll start dropping, reconnects hammer apiserver and etcd follower syncs.
dylan: short term: pause remaining drains and rollback the drainer rollout to v2.3.0. also bump NAT ephemeral ports on the gateway pool if possible.
maya: paused drains at 1778899032. rollback started.
sam: can we temporarily route GPU control-plane egress via eu fallback region for health checks? that reduces asia nat pressure while we stabilize.
jess: we can, but routing adds 150ms latency which may increase etcd election risk if we hit heartbeats. I'd rather reduce client fanout — lower kubelet apiserver QPS bursts for drains.
dylan: patch ready: reduce drainer parallelism from 4 -> 1 and increase gracePeriod to 120s. apply? snippet:
```
# drainer config
parallel: 1
gracePeriod: 120
```
maya: apply now and monitor etcd leader sync metric.
deploy-bot: rollback to v2.3.0 started at 1778899120 (batch 1/3).
sam: opened a short runbook note in #incidents: reduce-drain-fanout, nat-port-bump, rollback-drainer. assigning to @maya to validate metrics.
maya: watching etcd.appendEntriesDuration_seconds: went 2s -> 120ms after we paused.
jess: nice. next: long-term fix — add per-pool SNAT quotas (or use EIP per node), and change default drainer config for small pools (maxUnavailable absolute <2).
dylan: agreed. also need to add a preflight check in drainer: estimate outbound conn delta vs remaining SNAT capacity, fail drain if risk > 0.3.
maya: cost note: adding EIPs per gpu node increases baseline cost ~+7% for asia fleet. we should weigh against risk of more frequent throttles and failed rollouts.
sam: create a GH issue for cost/ops tradeoff and tag product infra-costs. recommend a short PoC in asia with 10 nodes EIP-backed.
maya: filing the issue now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/issue/4123
dylan: for immediate monitoring, add an alert: apiserver_fd_utilization > 0.8 for 2m -> page oncall.
jess: adding that alert and a dashboard panel for conntrack and apiserver 5xx.
maya: thanks all — keeping this thread for postmortem notes. will update once rollback fully finished.
(1778899810) deploy-bot: rollback completed (3/3). all drains paused. metrics stabilizing. :white_check_mark:
